name: Sovereign by Design: The Corponation Century
description: A sweeping, politically neutral-presenting historical account of the nation-state dissolution period from 2089-2161, tracing the legal, economic, and military mechanisms by which corponations achieved sovereign status in North America and the Pacific corridor. Produced by Vantablack Media's documentary wing with funding from a consortium of six corponations, the film is widely taught in Tier 3 corporate schools as authoritative history. Critics note the conspicuous absence of any testimony from communities displaced during sovereignty transitions.
cultural_impact: Defined the mainstream historical narrative of corponation formation for an entire generation of Tier 2-3 citizens, effectively replacing pre-collapse civic education curricula in most licensed school networks.
story_hooks: A historian discovers a scene in the documentary was filmed on location at a site that, according to sealed records, didn't exist until years after the depicted events.
The documentary's original director disappeared before final cut and the released version differs significantly from their recorded intentions.
A student assigned the documentary for corporate school finds annotations left by a previous viewer embedded in the holographic file's metadata layer.
